root.name: Tarrasch Defense: Prague Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 c5 4. cxd5 exd5 5. Nf3 Nc6 6. g3 Nf6

overview: White fianchettoes against the Tarrasch with 6.g3 and 7.Bg2, aiming to pressure d5. In the main line Black plays 7...cxd4 8.Nxd4 and 8...Be7 9.O-O O-O, leaving Black with an isolated d-pawn or a symmetrical-looking structure with active pieces. White tries to blockade and exploit the isolated d-pawn; Black counters with piece activity and ...Bg4 or ...Re8 ideas.

white_ideas.idea: Fianchetto and attack d5, then blockade the isolated pawn
Trade pieces to emphasise the isolated d-pawn weakness
Use Nxd4 and Nb3/Bf4-type moves to dominate the centre

black_ideas.idea: Active piece play to compensate for the isolated queen's pawn
Advance ...d4 or play ...Bg4/...Re8 and ...Bf8-g7 style activity
Avoid trades and keep pieces on to attack

typical_structures.structure: Isolated queen's pawn for Black on d5 against White's d4 gone
Hanging pawns c5/d5 if White avoids dxc5

character.notes: Dynamic Black piece activity versus a long-term structural weakness; not forcing but double-edged.

soundness.notes: Sound for both sides; main line of the Tarrasch.

structure.notes: Isolated d-pawn structure, partly open with a half-open c-file and e-file.

level.notes: IQP strategy is well known and the theory is moderate.

character.reason: Active Black pieces against a structural weakness; neither forcing nor passive.

soundness.reason: A main line of the Tarrasch.
